correctness.rationale: For the displayed morphism \(\sigma(a)=ab,\sigma(b)=ac,\sigma(c)=db,\sigma(d)=dc\), every image alternates \(A=\{a,d\}\) and \(B=\{b,c\}\). Injectivity of the first- and last-letter maps on each parity class reconstructs source factors from aligned and shifted windows. This proves \(P(2m)=P(m)+P(m+1)\) for \(m\ge2\), and \(P(2m+1)=2P(m+1)\) for \(m\ge1\); the initial values \(P(1)=4,P(2)=8\) imply \(P(n)=8(n-1)\) for \(n\ge2\). Every length-at-most-eight factor lies inside \(\sigma^3(xy)\) for one of eight proved adjacent pairs \(xy\); all eight pairs occur, so this union is exhaustive in the infinite fixed point. The 56 length-eight factors have no reversed partner; the four length-seven reversible factors are palindromes. A larger reversed pair would contain a reversed length-eight pair. The exact short table and \(R(n)=P(n)-(U_n-Q_n)/2\) finish the proof. The standalone checker actually returned `VERIFY_OK`; it confirms the factor-certificate SHA-256 and tests additional finite cases without substituting for the proof.

value.rationale: The unprojected four-state morphic cover of Rudin–Shapiro is a canonical natural automatic-sequence object, and reflection complexity is an established word invariant. The result exactly determines that invariant at every length and pins down the sharp threshold at eight with exceptional reversible palindromes; this is not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of the binary coding theorem. The nontrivial parity/injective-boundary mechanism also makes finite factor enumeration complete, providing a reusable structural tool for language analysis.
